name: Buckwheat Kasha with Mushrooms
reasons: Technique baked -> simmered; follow the stored preparation steps, not the dish title.

steps.display_text: Soak dried mushrooms in warm water for 20 minutes. Drain, reserving the liquid. Chop mushrooms.
Toast buckwheat in a dry pan for 2–3 minutes until aromatic.
Add mushroom soaking liquid and water (2 parts liquid to 1 part buckwheat). Bring to boil.
Add mushrooms, reduce heat, cover, and cook 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, caramelise diced onion in oil with garlic.
Fluff buckwheat, stir in caramelised onion. Season with salt and pepper.

name: Buckwheat with Fried Onion
reasons: Technique baked -> simmered; follow the stored preparation steps, not the dish title.

steps.display_text: Toast buckwheat in a dry pan for 2–3 minutes until it smells nutty.
Add boiling salted water (2:1 ratio). Cover and cook on lowest heat for 15 minutes. Do not lift the lid.
Meanwhile, slice onion thinly and fry in oil over medium heat for 15 minutes, stirring, until golden brown.
Fluff buckwheat with a fork and add a knob of butter.
Serve topped with caramelised onion. Great with a fried egg or sour cream.

name: Buffalo Chicken Wings
reasons: Technique fried -> baked; follow the stored preparation steps, not the dish title.
The oven step alone takes 45–50 min; allow 50 min plus the existing 13 min preparation.

steps.display_text: Pat wings dry. Toss with baking powder, salt, and garlic powder — this is key for crispiness.
Place on a rack over a tray. Bake at 200°C for 45–50 minutes, flipping halfway, until very crispy.
Make Buffalo sauce: melt butter and whisk in hot sauce (Frank's Red Hot) and a splash of vinegar.
Toss hot wings in Buffalo sauce until fully coated. Serve with celery sticks and blue cheese dip.

name: Burek
reasons: Technique fried -> baked; follow the stored preparation steps, not the dish title.
Remove the under-30 tag because corrected elapsed time exceeds 30 minutes.

steps.display_text: Make filling: brown beef mince with diced onion, season with salt and pepper. Cool.
Brush each filo sheet with oil. Spread a thin layer of meat filling along one edge.
Roll into a long thin log. Coil the log into a spiral in a greased round baking tin.
Repeat with remaining filo and filling, continuing the coil.
Brush top with oil or egg wash. Bake at 190°C for 35–40 minutes until deep golden brown.
Remove from oven and splash with cold water — this makes the pastry crispier. Rest 10 minutes. Serve with yogurt.

name: Burrito
reasons: Technique baked -> pan_fry; follow the stored preparation steps, not the dish title.

steps.display_text: Season and grill or pan-fry chicken breast until cooked through. Slice into strips.
Warm black beans with a pinch of cumin and salt.
Warm flour tortilla in a dry pan or microwave for 20 seconds to make it pliable.
Layer rice, beans, chicken, salsa, cheese, sour cream, and guacamole in the centre.
Fold the sides in, then roll tightly from the bottom up. Toast seam-side down in a pan for 1–2 minutes to seal.

name: Butter Naan
reasons: Include the mandatory 60 min dough rest.
Remove the under-30 tag because corrected elapsed time exceeds 30 minutes.

steps.display_text: Mix flour, yeast, sugar, salt, yogurt, and warm water. Knead into a soft dough. Rest covered for 1 hour.
Divide into balls. Roll each into a teardrop shape about 5 mm thick.
Heat a cast iron pan over maximum heat until very hot.
Place naan in the pan. Cook 1–2 minutes until large bubbles form on the surface.
Flip and cook 1 more minute until charred spots appear.
Brush immediately with garlic butter and scatter fresh cilantro. Serve hot.

name: Byrek (Albanian Filo Pie)
reasons: Technique fried -> baked; follow the stored preparation steps, not the dish title.
Remove the under-30 tag because corrected elapsed time exceeds 30 minutes.

steps.display_text: Wilt spinach in a hot pan. Squeeze out all moisture and chop roughly.
Mix spinach with crumbled white cheese, eggs, and olive oil. Season with salt.
Oil a round baking tin. Layer 3 filo sheets, brushing each with oil.
Spread spinach filling evenly. Layer 3 more oiled filo sheets on top.
Score the top and drizzle with oil. Bake at 190°C for 35–40 minutes until deep golden.
Splash with a little cold water when it comes out of the oven for extra crispness.

name: Börek Pita (Serbian Cheese Pie)
reasons: Technique fried -> baked; follow the stored preparation steps, not the dish title.

steps.display_text: Mix crumbled white cheese with eggs and sour cream. Season lightly (cheese is already salty).
Layer 2–3 oiled filo sheets in a baking tray. Spread cheese mixture over them.
Layer another 2–3 sheets on top, brushing each with oil.
Score the top layer into squares or diamonds. Drizzle with oil.
Bake at 190°C for 30–35 minutes until golden and flaky.
Let cool slightly. Traditionally splashed with cold water for extra flakiness.

name: Cheeseburger
reasons: Technique grilled -> pan_fry; follow the stored preparation steps, not the dish title.

steps.display_text: Form ground beef into a patty slightly larger than the bun (it will shrink). Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat a cast iron pan over high heat. Cook patty for 3–4 minutes per side for medium.
Place a slice of cheddar on the patty in the last minute. Cover to melt.
Toast bun halves in the same pan.
Build: sauce on bottom bun, lettuce, tomato, patty with cheese, pickles, top bun. Serve.

name: Cherry Varenyky
reasons: Technique baked -> boiled; follow the stored preparation steps, not the dish title.

steps.display_text: Make dough: combine flour, egg, a pinch of salt, and warm water. Knead until smooth and elastic. Rest 30 minutes.
Pit sour cherries. Toss with sugar and let sit 10 minutes — this draws out some juice.
Roll dough thin and cut circles with a glass. Place 3–4 cherries on each circle.
Pinch edges tightly to seal — cherry juice can cause them to open if not sealed well.
Boil in salted water for 5 minutes after they float. Serve with sour cream and a dusting of sugar.
